t: The Insurance Institute of India, which conducts the Licentiate, Associateship and Fellowship examinations and the IC-38 agents' examination, was established in:
o: 1972, at the nationalisation of general insurance
2000, by IRDA
1938, by the Insurance Act
1955, as the Federation of Insurance Institutes
e: The Insurance Institute of India was founded in 1955 (originally as the Federation of Insurance Institutes) and is headquartered in Mumbai, serving as the industry's professional education body.

t: Under the IRDAI (Micro Insurance) Regulations 2015, the maximum sum insured per asset/cover under a general micro-insurance product (e.g. dwelling, livestock, tools) is:
o: Rs 2 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 1 lakh
e: The 2015 regulations set the maximum sum insured for micro-insurance (life and general variants) at Rs 2 lakh (health cover per family also up to Rs 2 lakh).

t: Under the 2024 Regulations, the motor third party obligation applicable to general insurers requires each insurer to:
o: Refuse motor TP business beyond a limit
Transfer all motor TP business to the motor pool
Write at least 10% of its premium from motor TP
Underwrite a minimum percentage of motor third party business linked to its market share and the vehicles insured in the preceding year, including goods carrying and tractors
e: Section 32D and the 2024 Regulations prescribe minimum motor third party obligations for each general insurer, with specified shares of goods carrying vehicles, tractors and other categories.

t: Under the IRDAI Master Guidelines on AML/CFT 2022, a 'Politically Exposed Person' (PEP) is defined as:
o: A person holding more than Rs 1 crore in insurance policies
Any member of a political party

An individual who is or has been entrusted with prominent public functions by a foreign country, including heads of state, senior politicians, senior government/judicial/military officers and senior executives of state-owned corporations
Any Government employee
e: The PML Rules definition of PEP (as amended in 2023) covers individuals entrusted with prominent public functions by a foreign country; insurers must apply enhanced due diligence and senior management approval for PEPs.

t: Under the IRDAI (Registration of Insurance Marketing Firm) Regulations 2015, an IMF may engage in which of the following activities?
o: Issuing surveyor licences
Solicitation of insurance products through Insurance Sales Persons, insurance servicing activities, and distribution of other financial products such as mutual funds, NPS and bank products
Underwriting and claims settlement for insurers
Reinsurance broking
e: IMFs are permitted to solicit insurance, provide insurance service activities (survey, TPA-like services) and distribute other regulated financial products like mutual funds, pension products and banking products.

t: Kiran drives his car without a valid third-party insurance policy and is stopped by police. Under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (as amended in 2019), the penalty for the first offence of driving without insurance is:
o: Fine up to Rs 500
Imprisonment up to three months and/or fine of Rs 2,000 (Rs 4,000 for a subsequent offence)
Fine of Rs 10,000 only
Cancellation of the vehicle registration
e: Section 196 (as amended in 2019) prescribes imprisonment up to three months or a fine of Rs 2,000 or both for a first offence, and Rs 4,000 for a subsequent offence.

t: Suresh wants to file a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman but the same matter is already pending before a consumer commission. Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017:
o: The complaint is not maintainable before the Ombudsman while the same subject matter is pending before any court, consumer forum or arbitrator
The Ombudsman will transfer the case from the consumer commission
The complaint can be filed only after the consumer commission's decision is set aside
The Ombudsman can still entertain the complaint
e: Rule 14 provides that a complaint is not maintainable if the same subject matter is pending or has been decided by a court, consumer forum or arbitrator.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Web Aggregators) Regulations 2017, a web aggregator is permitted to:
o: Collect premium in its own bank account and remit later
Underwrite insurance risks
Display comparative information on insurance products of different insurers on its website and solicit insurance online/telemarketing as a lead provider
Issue policies in its own name
e: Web aggregators maintain websites providing product comparison and act as lead generators and distributors through online, tele-marketing and distance marketing modes.

t: Under Section 5 of the IRDA Act 1999, the Chairperson of IRDAI holds office for a term of:
o: Five years or until age 65, whichever is earlier
Five years or until age 62, whichever is earlier
Three years, renewable once
Six years with no age limit
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 5 provides a five-year term for the Chairperson subject to a maximum age of 65 years; whole-time members hold office for five years or till age 62.

t: Following the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019, an application for compensation before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal under Section 166 must be made within:
o: Three years of the accident
No time limit, as before
Six months of the occurrence of the accident
One year of the accident
e: Section 166(3), reintroduced in 2019, requires the claim application to be filed within six months of the accident; the earlier Act had removed any limitation.

t: Under the IRDAI Surveyors Regulations, a surveyor must submit the survey report to the insurer, in a non-complex case, within:
o: 30 days of appointment
60 days of appointment
7 days of appointment
15 days of appointment
e: The surveyor must submit the final report within 15 days of appointment (30 days for complex cases) and must not delay or withhold the report.

t: Under Section 110 of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015), an appeal against an order of IRDAI must be filed with the Securities Appellate Tribunal within:
o: 90 days from the date of the order
30 days from the date on which a copy of the order is received
45 days from the date on which a copy of the order is received
60 days from the date of the order
e: Section 110 provides that an appeal lies to the SAT within 45 days of receipt of the order, with power to condone delay for sufficient cause.

t: Before its omission in 2015, Section 40A of the Insurance Act 1938 mainly dealt with:
o: Investment of controlled funds
Prohibition of rebating
Limits on commission payable to insurance agents for life and general insurance
Minimum paid-up capital of insurers
e: Section 40A prescribed statutory ceilings on agency commission (e.g. 35% first-year for life); it was omitted by the 2015 amendment and commission limits are now governed by IRDAI regulations.

t: Section 64VC of the Insurance Act 1938 provides that an insurer shall not open a new place of business or relocate an existing one in India without:
o: Approval of the Reserve Bank of India
Prior permission of IRDAI, subject to the Authority's regulations/guidelines
A resolution of the State Legislature
Consent of the Life Insurance Council
e: Section 64VC restricts opening or shifting of places of business without IRDAI permission; IRDAI has since liberalised this via regulations and board-approved policies.

t: Under Section 102 of the Insurance Act 1938, penalties collected by IRDAI are credited to:
o: The Consumer Welfare Fund
The Policyholders' Protection Fund
The IRDAI Fund under Section 16
The Consolidated Fund of India
e: Section 102 (and Section 105C) provide that penalties imposed under the Act are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India, not retained by IRDAI.

t: The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015 raised the permissible foreign investment in an Indian insurance company from 26% to:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2015 amendment to Section 2(7A) of the Insurance Act raised the composite foreign investment cap from 26% to 49%, subject to the company being Indian owned and controlled.

t: Under the PPHI Regulations 2024, a general insurer must appoint a surveyor for a claim within how many hours of receipt of claim intimation?
o: 12 hours
24 hours
48 hours
72 hours
e: The 2024 regulations require a general insurer to allocate a surveyor within 24 hours of claim intimation, with the survey report to be submitted within 15 days of allocation.

t: Under the Corporate Agents Regulations 2015, the employees of a corporate agent who solicit and procure insurance business are called:
o: Specified Persons, who must pass the prescribed examination
Insurance Marketing Executives
Point of Sales Persons
Agents
e: Specified Persons are employees of a corporate agent who have passed the specified examination and are authorised to solicit insurance on behalf of the corporate agent.

t: Under Section 20 of the Marine Insurance Act 1963, a contract of marine insurance is a contract based upon utmost good faith, and if the utmost good faith is not observed by either party:
o: The insurer must pay double the sum insured
Only the premium is refunded
The contract is automatically void and premium forfeited
The contract may be avoided by the other party
e: Section 20 provides that marine insurance is a contract of utmost good faith and that non-observance by either party entitles the other party to avoid the contract.

t: Under the IRDAI (Outsourcing of Activities by Indian Insurers) Regulations 2017, the responsibility for outsourced activities lies with:
o: The insurer and its board, which remain fully responsible for the outsourced activity
IRDAI
The policyholder
The service provider
e: The regulations make clear that outsourcing does not diminish the insurer's obligations; the board and senior management remain accountable for all outsourced functions.

t: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 enables consumer disputes to be referred to mediation. Which of the following is correct?
o: Mediation is permitted only for claims above Rs 1 crore
Mediation is compulsory for all insurance complaints
The Commission may refer a dispute to a Consumer Mediation Cell attached to it, with the consent of the parties, where settlement appears possible
Mediation is conducted only by the Insurance Ombudsman
e: Chapter V of the 2019 Act provides for Consumer Mediation Cells attached to each Commission, to which disputes may be referred with the parties' consent.

t: Under Section 6A(4)(b) of the Insurance Act 1938, prior approval of IRDAI is required for any transfer of shares of an insurer where the transfer results in a holding of more than what percentage of paid-up capital?
o: 10 percent
26 percent
1 percent
5 percent
e: Section 6A(4)(b) requires IRDAI's prior approval for a transfer of shares where the nominal value transferred exceeds 1% of paid-up capital, or where the transferee would hold more than 5% of paid-up capital.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, how many Insurance Ombudsman offices currently operate across India?
e: There are 17 Insurance Ombudsman centres across India (including Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Noida, Patna and Pune).

t: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act 1991, the owner of a hazardous substance must pay a contribution equal to the premium into which fund?
o: Environment Relief Fund, established under Section 7A
National Disaster Response Fund
Policyholders' Protection Fund
Consolidated Fund of India
e: Section 4(2C) requires the owner to pay an amount equal to the premium to the Environment Relief Fund established under Section 7A, in addition to the premium to the insurer.

t: Under the amended Section 39 of the Insurance Act 1938, a nominee who is the parent, spouse or child of the policyholder is treated as a:
o: Trustee nominee
Collector nominee
Beneficial nominee entitled to the policy proceeds
Conditional assignee
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 39(7), inserted by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015, makes parents, spouse and children beneficial nominees who are beneficially entitled to the amount payable, not merely receivers on behalf of legal heirs.

t: Under Section 6 of the IRDA Act 1999, the Central Government may remove a member of IRDAI from office if the member:
o: Is adjudged insolvent, is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, or acquires a financial interest likely to affect prejudicially his functions
Expresses disagreement with the Chairperson in a meeting
Is more than 55 years of age
Takes leave for more than 30 days
e: Section 6 lists grounds for removal including insolvency, incapacity, conviction for moral turpitude, acquiring prejudicial financial interest and abuse of position.

t: Rohit returned his life policy within the free-look period citing dissatisfaction with the terms. Under the PPHI Regulations 2024, the insurer must refund the premium:
o: Only in the form of a credit towards another policy
In full without any deduction
After deducting proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, expenses incurred on medical examination and stamp duty charges
After deducting 50% as administrative charges
e: On free-look cancellation, the insurer refunds the premium less proportionate risk premium for the cover period, medical examination expenses and stamp duty.

t: Under Section 4 of the IRDA Act 1999, the members of the Authority other than the Chairperson consist of:
o: Only part-time members nominated by State Governments
Not more than five whole-time members and not more than four part-time members
Exactly ten whole-time members
Not more than three whole-time members and not more than two part-time members
e: Section 4 provides for a Chairperson, not more than five whole-time members and not more than four part-time members, all appointed by the Central Government.

t: An individual agent appointed by a life insurer and a general insurer wishes to also represent a mono-line insurer (e.g. an agricultural insurance company). Under the Agents Regulations 2016 this is:
o: Permitted only if the agent surrenders the general insurance agency
Not permitted, as the agent can represent only two insurers
Permitted, as an agent may represent one life, one general, one health and one of each mono-line insurer
Permitted only with IRDAI's prior approval in each case
e: Regulation 6 allows an individual agent to be appointed by one life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer and one of each mono-line insurer.

t: Under the Reinsurance Regulations 2018, the first preference in the order of cession (after obligatory cession) is to be given to:
o: Foreign reinsurer branches (FRBs) in IFSC
Lloyd's syndicates abroad
Cross-border reinsurers rated AAA
Indian reinsurers (such as GIC Re) that have been in business for at least three continuous years
e: The order of preference starts with Indian reinsurers with three years of continuous operations, then FRBs/IIOs, then CBRs, with the 2018 regulations later relaxed to allow simultaneous offers to multiple categories.

t: Under the IRDAI (Third Party Administrators - Health Services) Regulations 2016, the certificate of registration of a TPA is valid for:
o: Three years
Five years
Perpetual validity subject to annual fee
One year
e: The TPA registration is valid for three years and renewable on application; the 2016 regulations also require a minimum capital of Rs 4 crore and a working capital of Rs 1 crore.

t: Under Sections 64C and 64L of the Insurance Act 1938, the functions of the Life Insurance Council and General Insurance Council include:
o: Issuing certificates of registration to insurers
Aiding, advising and assisting insurers in setting up sound business practices, rendering advice to IRDAI, and bringing to the Authority's notice any undesirable practice
Fixing premium rates for all products
Appointing the Insurance Ombudsman
e: The Councils, constituted under Section 64C, function under Section 64F/64L to promote sound practices, advise the Authority and act as self-regulatory industry bodies, with executive committees for each.

t: Section 103 of the Insurance Act 1938 prescribes the penalty for carrying on insurance business in contravention of Sections 3, 7 or 98 (i.e., without registration or deposit). The penalty may extend to:
o: Rs 25 crore and imprisonment up to 10 years
Rs 1 lakh per day up to Rs 1 crore and imprisonment up to 10 years
Rs 10 lakh only
Rs 1 lakh per day up to Rs 1 crore
e: Section 103 (as amended in 2015) provides for a penalty which may extend to Rs 25 crore and imprisonment which may extend to ten years for carrying on business without registration.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
o: Unlimited
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: Under the Brokers Regulations 2018, a direct broker is permitted to:
o: Arrange reinsurance for insurers
Solicit and arrange insurance business for its clients with insurers and provide claims consultancy and risk management services
Underwrite insurance risks on behalf of insurers
Issue cover notes in its own name
e: A direct broker represents clients in arranging life and/or general insurance with insurers, and may also offer claims consultancy and risk management, but cannot deal in reinsurance.

t: Under IRDAI health insurance norms, a health insurer must offer policy renewal, portability and migration options; the portability request must be made at least how many days before renewal?
o: 45 days
60 days
15 days
30 days
e: A policyholder seeking portability must apply to the new insurer at least 45 days (but not more than 60 days) before the premium renewal date.

t: Section 31B of the Insurance Act 1938 empowers IRDAI to regulate:
o: The remuneration (including non-cash perquisites) payable to the directors, managing agents, chief executives and senior officers of an insurer
The premium rates for motor third party insurance
The minimum qualification of surveyors
The maximum commission payable to agents
e: Section 31B prohibits an insurer from paying remuneration to directors, managers or officers in excess of limits prescribed by IRDAI, and requires prior approval for MD/CEO remuneration.

t: Under the IRDAI Brokers Regulations 2018, the 'Principal Officer' of an insurance broker must:
o: Be a chartered accountant
Possess the prescribed qualification and have undergone 50 hours training (direct broker) and passed the examination conducted by the specified institute
Be a director of at least one insurance company
Have a licence as a surveyor
e: The Principal Officer must meet eligibility criteria including qualifications, broker training and examination (50 hours for direct brokers, more for reinsurance/composite).

t: Under the IRDAI (Bima Vahaks) Guidelines 2023, a 'Bima Vahak' is:
o: A vehicle used for insurance awareness rallies
A women-centric distribution channel at gram panchayat level to distribute and service insurance (including Bima Vistaar)
A claims tribunal for motor accidents
A reinsurance intermediary
e: Bima Vahaks are individual/corporate field-level distributors, with a focus on women, engaged at gram panchayat level to improve insurance reach in rural India.

t: Under Section 18 of the IRDA Act 1999, the Authority is bound by directions on questions of policy given by:
o: The Supreme Court of India
The Life Insurance Council
The Reserve Bank of India
The Central Government, after giving the Authority an opportunity to express its views
e: Section 18 provides that IRDAI is bound by Central Government directions on policy questions (other than technical and administrative matters), and the Government's decision on what is a policy question is final.

t: Under the IRDAI (Expenses of Management, including Commission, of Insurers) Regulations 2023, the overall expenses of management limit for a life insurer, as a percentage of total premium, is broadly:
o: Up to 15% of total premium
A single overall limit of 30% of premium computed per segment-wise allowable limits
Up to 50% of total premium
No limit applies
e: The 2023 EoM regulations replaced granular product-wise commission caps with an overall EoM limit (life insurers have segment-wise allowable limits aggregating to an overall ceiling; general/health insurers 30%/35%).

t: IRDAI monitors solvency through periodic returns. Under Section 64VA of the Insurance Act 1938, if an insurer fails to maintain the required solvency margin, IRDAI may:
o: Suspend the insurer's board for 10 years
Impose a fine on the policyholders
Direct the insurer to submit a financial plan indicating a plan of action to correct the deficiency within a specified period, and if inadequate, treat it as a ground for cancellation of registration
Transfer the insurer's policies to LIC
e: Section 64VA requires a deficient insurer to submit a financial plan on IRDAI's direction; failure to meet the control level of solvency can lead to regulatory action including cancellation.

t: Section 6A of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that the paid-up share capital of a public company carrying on insurance business must consist of:
o: Debentures convertible into equity within five years
Equity shares with differential voting rights to protect promoters
Only equity shares each having a single face value
Equity shares and redeemable preference shares in equal proportion
e: Section 6A provides that the capital of an Indian insurance company shall consist only of ordinary (equity) shares, each of which has a single face value, with voting rights restricted to equity shares.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

t: Under the 2024 Health Insurance master circular, if a policyholder dies during treatment, the insurer must:
o: Immediately process the claim settlement request and release the mortal remains from the hospital without delay
Wait for the legal heir certificate before releasing the body
Refer the matter to the TPA for a 30-day review
Treat the claim as void
e: The master circular directs insurers to immediately process claim settlement and ensure the mortal remains are released without delay when a policyholder dies during treatment.

t: Under the IRDAI Registration of Indian Insurance Companies Regulations 2022, the promoter lock-in period for shares held in a newly registered insurer is:
o: Five years from the date of grant of certificate of registration
Ten years from the date of grant of certificate of registration
No lock-in applies
Three years from the date of registration
e: The 2022 regulations prescribe a lock-in of promoter shareholding for five years from grant of registration (longer lock-in for promoters coming in later via regulated transfers).

t: Under the IRDAI (Appointment of Insurance Agents) Regulations 2016, the designated official of an insurer who issues appointment letters to agents is called the:
o: Principal Officer
Designated Official
Chief Agency Manager
Development Officer
e: Each insurer must nominate a Designated Official responsible for issuing appointment letters and maintaining records of agents under the 2016 regulations.

t: Which of the following is NOT among the duties, powers and functions of IRDAI enumerated in Section 14(2) of the IRDA Act 1999?
o: Fixing the rate of income tax on insurance companies
Specifying the percentage of life and general insurance business to be undertaken in the rural or social sector
Specifying the code of conduct for surveyors and loss assessors
Regulating investment of funds by insurance companies
e: Section 14(2) covers registration, policyholder protection, codes of conduct, investment regulation, solvency, rural/social sector percentages and more; taxation is outside IRDAI's remit.

t: Which of the following statements about statutory deposits under Section 7 of the Insurance Act 1938 is correct after the 2015 amendment?
o: The deposit requirement applies only to foreign reinsurer branches
Deposits may be made only in gold held with a scheduled bank
Every insurer must deposit Rs 10 crore in cash with the RBI
The deposit requirement was made subject to IRDAI regulations rather than fixed amounts in the Act
e: The 2015 amendment substituted Section 7 so that the deposit to be kept with RBI is as specified by IRDAI regulations, replacing the earlier fixed amounts tied to premium income.

t: Section 48A of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits an insurance agent or intermediary from being:
o: A director of an insurance company
A member of a chamber of commerce
A policyholder of the same insurer
A shareholder of the insurer
e: Section 48A bars insurance agents and intermediaries from being directors of insurance companies, except as permitted with IRDAI approval under the proviso.
